flawed_step: The shortest remaining interval need not belong to any maximum-size schedule; choosing it can eliminate two mutually compatible intervals.
counterexample: Take A=[2,4), B=[0,3), and C=[3,7), with distinct durations 2, 3, and 4. The greedy rule must choose A first. A conflicts with both B and C, so they are discarded and the greedy schedule has size 1. But B and C are non-overlapping because the intervals are half-open and B ends exactly when C starts, so {B,C} is a schedule of size 2, which is optimal.
assessment_summary: The rule returns 1 interval while the optimum returns 2. Distinct durations make tie-breaking irrelevant.
